policy: Only exercises from the uploaded textbook are used. Numerical data and required mathematical tasks are retained; MCQ options and explanatory solutions are added. Supplementary same-outcome book exercises are explicitly identified in LO references. Practice marks and 60-minute timing are not official exam settings.
selection_basis: Prioritise explicitly cited exercises, misconception checks, and complementary representations. No prediction or probability claim about the actual government final exam.

learning_outcomes.title: FOIL binomial products
learning_outcomes.statement: Multiply binomials by using the FOIL method.
learning_outcomes.rule_summary: Multiply all four pairs, then combine the two middle terms.

learning_outcomes.title: Squares of sums and differences
learning_outcomes.statement: Find squares of sums and differences.
learning_outcomes.rule_summary: (a ± b)² = a² ± 2ab + b². Do not omit the middle term.

learning_outcomes.title: Sum and difference products
learning_outcomes.statement: Find the product of a sum and a difference.
learning_outcomes.rule_summary: (a+b)(a−b)=a²−b²; the middle terms cancel.

learning_outcomes.title: Factor using distribution
learning_outcomes.statement: Factor polynomials by using the Distributive Property.
learning_outcomes.rule_summary: Take the greatest common factor from every term; check by multiplication.

learning_outcomes.title: Analyse monic trinomial factors
learning_outcomes.statement: Factor trinomials of the form x² + bx + c.
learning_outcomes.rule_summary: For (x+r)(x+s), r+s=b and rs=c. Enumerate integer factor pairs.

learning_outcomes.title: Factor non-monic trinomials
learning_outcomes.statement: Factor trinomials of the form ax² + bx + c.
learning_outcomes.rule_summary: Find two numbers with product ac and sum b; split the middle term and group.

learning_outcomes.title: Difference of squares
learning_outcomes.statement: Factor binomials that are the difference of squares.
learning_outcomes.rule_summary: A²−B²=(A−B)(A+B). Factor repeatedly when possible.

learning_outcomes.title: Divide monomials
learning_outcomes.statement: Divide monomials using the properties of exponents.
learning_outcomes.rule_summary: Subtract exponents when dividing; multiply every exponent when raising a quotient to a power.

learning_outcomes.title: Negative and zero exponents
learning_outcomes.statement: Simplify expressions containing negative and zero exponents.
learning_outcomes.rule_summary: For a≠0, a⁰=1 and a⁻ⁿ=1/aⁿ. Move only factors with negative exponents.

learning_outcomes.title: Rational exponents
learning_outcomes.statement: Evaluate and rewrite expressions involving rational exponents.
learning_outcomes.rule_summary: a^(1/n) is the principal nth root of a. Evaluate the root before any other power.

learning_outcomes.title: Products of square roots
learning_outcomes.statement: Simplify radical expressions by using the Product Property of Square Roots.
learning_outcomes.rule_summary: √a·√b=√(ab) for a,b≥0. Extract perfect-square factors; area uses the full formula.

learning_outcomes.title: Quotients of radicals
learning_outcomes.statement: Simplify radical expressions by using the Quotient Property of Square Roots.
learning_outcomes.rule_summary: √(a/b)=√a/√b for a≥0,b>0. Simplify and rationalise the denominator. For cube roots, extract cubes.

learning_outcomes.title: Add and subtract radicals
learning_outcomes.statement: Add and subtract radical expressions.
learning_outcomes.rule_summary: Simplify the radicals first; combine coefficients only when their radicands match.

learning_outcomes.title: Factoring in context
learning_outcomes.statement: Solve quadratic equations by factoring.
learning_outcomes.rule_summary: Set a physical model equal to the required height/volume, factor, then reject roots outside its domain.

learning_outcomes.title: Square root and completing-square methods
learning_outcomes.statement: Solve quadratic equations using the Square Root Property and by completing the square.
learning_outcomes.rule_summary: Isolate (x−h)²; take both square roots. Complete the square by adding (b/2)².

learning_outcomes.title: Translations of quadratics
learning_outcomes.statement: Write a quadratic in vertex form and transform its graph.
learning_outcomes.rule_summary: In y=a(x−h)²+k, the vertex is (h,k). x−h shifts right; x+h shifts left.

learning_outcomes.title: Factoring quadratic equations
learning_outcomes.statement: Solve quadratic equations by factoring.
learning_outcomes.rule_summary: Write one side as zero, factor fully, and apply the zero-product property. Check every root.

learning_outcomes.title: Dilations and reflections of quadratics
learning_outcomes.statement: Write quadratics in vertex form and transform their graphs.
learning_outcomes.rule_summary: A negative outside coefficient reflects across the x-axis; |a|>1 stretches vertically. Simplify an inside coefficient before comparing.

learning_outcomes.title: Solve quadratics by graphing
learning_outcomes.statement: Solve quadratic equations by graphing.
learning_outcomes.rule_summary: Real solutions are the x-intercepts of the related graph; a tangent gives a repeated root; no intersection means no real solution.

learning_outcomes.title: Complete the square
learning_outcomes.statement: Solve quadratic equations by completing the square.
learning_outcomes.rule_summary: First make the coefficient of x² equal to 1. Add (b/2)² to form a perfect square.

learning_outcomes.title: Add and subtract polynomials
learning_outcomes.statement: Add and subtract polynomials.
learning_outcomes.rule_summary: Distribute a subtraction sign to every term; then collect like terms.

learning_outcomes.title: Multiply polynomials
learning_outcomes.statement: Multiply polynomials by using the Distributive Property.
learning_outcomes.rule_summary: Multiply each term in the first polynomial by every term in the second; collect equal powers.

learning_outcomes.title: Multiplication properties of exponents
learning_outcomes.statement: Multiply monomials and simplify expressions using multiplication properties of exponents.
learning_outcomes.rule_summary: Add exponents in a product; multiply exponents in a power. Apply the power to the coefficient too.

learning_outcomes.title: Quadratic extrema and graph features
learning_outcomes.statement: Find and interpret maximum and minimum values of a quadratic function.
learning_outcomes.rule_summary: The vertex (h,k) gives the minimum k when the graph opens up and maximum k when it opens down; the axis is x=h.

learning_outcomes.title: Write a quadratic from its graph
learning_outcomes.statement: Write quadratic equations using Standard Form.
learning_outcomes.rule_summary: Read the zeros r,s, write y=a(x−r)(x−s), then use another point to find a. Expand to y=ax²+bx+c.

questions.stem: Consider the two expressions. (m^p)(m^q)\quad\text{and}\quad(m^p)^q

parts.prompt: What must be true about p and q for the expressions to be equal? Give an example.

answer.model_answer_and_marking: For positive m≠1, require p+q=pq, or (p−1)(q−1)=1 (3). Example p=q=2 (2). Without that assumption, m=1 makes both expressions equal for all defined p,q; other bases require domain care.

parts.prompt: Assuming m, p and q are positive integers, can (mᵖ)(mᑫ) > (mᵖ)ᑫ ever be true? Explain.

answer.model_answer_and_marking: Yes. Take m=2 and p=q=1: 2·2=4>2¹=2 (3). For m>1 compare exponents p+q and pq (2).
